_comment: Documented divergences of the JVM pattern-safety chain against the safety_gates corpus. Fail-closed: a failing case NOT listed here is red; a listed case that now reproduces the reference verdict is red (stale baseline); a listed case whose observed divergent verdict no longer matches the recorded one is red (drifted entry). All six entries are cost-verdict-mode TIMING facts: the corpus oracle is Python re + the reference synthesizer on the generating host, and the extrapolated cost of the synthesized probe sets is measured on THIS engine's executor (java.util.regex backtracking under the DeadlineCharSequence abort). The structural, compile, dangerous-construct and test-string probe layers reproduce every reference verdict (88/94 exact). Entry format: '<observed safe>,<observed reason_class> :: <written reason>'.

cases.safety_gates/safety_cost_verdict_over_bu: safe=true,safe :: reference over-budget is a Python-re timing fact: (\d|\w)*; extrapolates past the 0.05s budget on the reference engine while java.util.regex executes the same probe sets far under the normalized budget, so the JVM arbiter accepts. The Rust family ledgered the identical case for the identical reason (its regex-crate NFA is also faster than Python re).
cases.safety_gates/safety_cost_verdict_structu: safe=true,safe :: reference rejects (a|aa)+$ because its probe timing on Python re crosses the budget and the nested-unbounded structural flag rides the over-budget reason; the JVM synthesizer reaches the pattern and java.util.regex times it under budget at the same cap, so the per-engine cost verdict accepts. Same root cause as the Rust family's ledger entry.
cases.safety_gates/safety_cost_verdict_safe_05: safe=false,structural_unreachable_terminator :: opposite-direction timing fact: on java.util.regex the greedy char-class backtrack over the prefix-flood probes measures right at the 0.05s budget boundary at cap 10000 (extrapolated ~0.05-0.07s across runs), so an over-budget probe set returns the structural violation; Python re backtracks the same probes under budget and accepts. Borderline by construction: the Go family logged this exact case flipping once under host load on its engine.
cases.safety_gates/safety_cost_verdict_safe_06: safe=false,structural_unreachable_terminator :: java.util.regex measures the <script[^>]*> probe sets at extrapolated 0.057-0.066s vs the 0.05s budget (min 0.59-0.69s at 32000 chars, host-load normalized) where Python re measures under; the over-budget probe set returns the structural violation and the case rejects where the reference accepts.
cases.safety_gates/safety_cost_verdict_safe_08: safe=false,structural_unreachable_terminator :: java.util.regex measures the \$\([^)]+\) probe sets at extrapolated ~0.19-0.20s, 4x the 0.05s budget, where Python re measures under; the rejection reason is the structural unreachable-terminator text riding the over-budget probe set.
cases.safety_gates/safety_cost_verdict_safe_09: safe=false,structural_unreachable_terminator :: java.util.regex measures the \$\{[^}]+\} probe sets at extrapolated ~0.198-0.202s, 4x the 0.05s budget, where Python re measures under; same divergence class as safety_cost_verdict_safe_08.
